terms.comment: “Attic” is a modern application (Traupman). The ancient adjective’s sense is clear: Pliny, NH 36.185 has pavīmenta … barbarica atque subtēgulānea, floors under the roof, i.e. indoors (Lewis & Short: “that is under the roof, = in-doors”). An older Morgan draft called Pliny’s sense uncertain; the passage settles it.

phrases.english: a room under the roof, a loft room

subtegulaneum.against: Lewis & Short sub-tĕgŭlānĕus, against its own tēgula
subtegulaneum.html: The word is built on tēgula, which Lewis & Short marks long (s.v. tēgulae); the ē of tēgula is kept.

sources: Lewis & Short: subtegulaneus · Morgan–Owens: furnished attic · Morgan–Owens: garret attic room · Older Morgan draft: attic caveat
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 122.
